world: O ORDINAL-ONLY (point estimates) / UNVERIFIED between M and O
outcome_variable_scope: r30's stored source-specificity shares for two donor conditions under three judge families, on 300 prompts. Nothing is recomputed and no judge is added.
scope: Settles the ORDINAL question and leaves the CARDINAL one UNVERIFIED for want of joint bootstrap draws. It also inherits r30's own stated gap: no phi cell was ever measured at the farthest-donor floor, so the grid's upper corner is unobserved and this test covers the two donor conditions that exist in all three judges.
verdict: O ORDINAL-ONLY (point estimates) / UNVERIFIED between M and O. Every attack this session tested the framing of what REMAINS; none tested the framing itself. M(R,J,pi,Q,P) with 'each layer validated separately' PRESUMES the layers are separable, and r30's grid can put that to a test the release already paid for. RESULT (a), WHICH IS CLEAN: the near<random ordering holds in 3 of 3 judges -- all of them. So the rubric's ordinal property survives a change of judge, and the world in which there is no judge-invariant property at all is REFUTED at the ordinal level. The null is weak and is reported as weak: with 3 judges, P(all agree by chance) = 0.25, which is evidence and not proof. RESULT (b), WHICH IS THE FINDING: the near/random ratio is 0.539, 0.567, 0.735 -- a 1.36x spread. If the judge were a pure multiplicative GAIN that ratio would be constant, and R would be separable from J up to scale. It is not constant in the point estimates. BUT THIS CANNOT BE SETTLED HERE, AND THE REASON IS A STORAGE GAP RATHER THAN A DATA LIMIT: the paired ratio's sampling distribution needs the JOINT bootstrap draws, and r30 persisted only the rep count (`boot` = 8000) with marginal CIs. Marginal CIs cannot substitute, because r30's own note records that the bootstrap resampled prompts JOINTLY across numerator and denominator -- the arms are correlated by construction, so marginal intervals overstate the ratio's uncertainty by an unknown amount, in the direction that would make a real interaction look untestable. VERDICT IS THREE-VALUED AND UNVERIFIED IS NOT AN ACQUITTAL: the multiplicative world is neither confirmed nor excluded. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT, priced rather than wished for: re-running the SAME three judges on the SAME 300 prompts and persisting per-draw ratios. That is not 'more judges', which is frozen -- it is the panel already frozen by r80, re-scored to store what r30 discarded. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FRAMING: layer-at-a-time validation is defensible for ORDINAL claims about R and is UNVERIFIED for CARDINAL ones, which is exactly the distinction the headline already draws between an ordering and a share -- reached here from the separability side rather than the floor side.
